domain: Race, stratification & economic disparities in the United States
source_registry: Adapted from the DuBois project registry (0.1.0, 2026-07-27) for the public Anu replication package.

series.title: US Total Population
series.description: Annual US resident population, 1790-2024. The demographic backbone for per-capita and share calculations across panels.

source.name: MeasuringWorth (Samuel H. Williamson, 'What Was the U.S. GDP Then?'), population column
source.license: Free for research use; cite Williamson (see site terms)

construction.method: Annual population column extracted from the MeasuringWorth USGDP dataset (manual CSV download); decennial values cross-validated against Census HSUS 1975 Series A 1-8 as-enumerated values (agreement >= 99.5%).

series.title: US Population by Race (shares)
series.description: Population counts and percentage shares by race (B02001 'alone' universe) with a separate Hispanic cross-tab (B03002), 2005-2022.

source.name: US Census Bureau, ACS 1-Year Estimates (B02001, B03002) via Census API

construction.method: API pull of national race counts; shares computed as category/total x 100 per year. Race is 'alone' universe; Hispanic reported as separate ethnicity, never merged into race.

series.title: Median Net Worth by Race
series.description: Weighted median (and mean) household net worth by race, from all 12 triennial SCF waves 1989-2022. The site's headline wealth panel.

source.name: Federal Reserve, Survey of Consumer Finances (SCF) summary microdata files, 12 waves

construction.method: Sample-weighted (WGT) medians/means per race per wave over all five implicates. Race coding harmonized across waves (Asian reported only for 2022; not back-imputed).

series.units: US dollars, current (nominal) per survey wave

series.title: Black Wealth as % of White
series.description: Black and Hispanic median net worth as a percent of White median net worth, per SCF wave 1989-2022, with dollar gaps.

source.name: Derived from Federal Reserve SCF (see D1003)

construction.method: Ratio of weighted medians per wave (black_median/white_median x 100); gap = white - black. Computed per wave from microdata, never spliced from growth rates.

quality.notes: 1989 value (6.0%) verified as a genuine early-SCF small-sample/race-coding artifact, not a pipeline bug; excluded from trend claims (cite 1992-2022).

series.title: Unemployment Rate by Race
series.description: Annual average unemployment rates by race (White 1954+, Black 1972+, Hispanic 1973+, Asian 2000+), from monthly CPS series.

source.name: BLS Current Population Survey via FRED (LNS14000003, LNS14000006, LNS14000009, LNS14032183)

construction.method: Keyless FRED CSV download of the four monthly SA series; annual averages computed in P03. Pre-1972 Black / pre-1973 Hispanic / pre-2000 Asian coverage is absent (not collected), never back-imputed.

series.title: Black/White Unemployment Ratio
series.description: Black unemployment rate relative to White, annually 1972-2025. Documents the persistent ~2x multiplier.

source.name: Derived from BLS CPS via FRED (see D1005)

construction.method: Ratio of annual averages (Black/White); recession-episode peaks identified against NBER peak-trough dates.

series.title: Median Household Income by Race
series.description: Median household income by race, ACS 1-Year 2005-2022, nominal and deflated to 2022 dollars with CPI-U.

source.name: US Census Bureau, ACS 1-Year B19013 (+A/B/C/D/H/I race iterations) via Census API; CPI-U (CPIAUCSL) via FRED

construction.method: API pull per year/race; real values = nominal x (CPI_2022 / CPI_year) using annual-average CPIAUCSL. 2020 absent (ACS 1-year cancelled, COVID); not imputed.

series.title: Poverty Rate by Race
series.description: Share of population below poverty by race (B17001), with Black/White and Hispanic/White gaps and ratios, 2005-2022.

source.name: US Census Bureau, ACS 1-Year B17001 (+race iterations) via Census API

construction.method: poverty_rate = B17001{su}_002E / B17001{su}_001E per year and race; gaps in percentage points, ratios of rates.

series.title: Bachelor's+ Attainment by Race
series.description: Share of population 25+ with a bachelor's degree or higher by race (C15002), with Black/White gaps and ratios.

source.name: US Census Bureau, ACS 1-Year C15002 (+race iterations) via Census API

construction.method: bachelor's+ = pre-summed degree columns per sex in the C15002 race iterations (_006E male + _011E female) / total 25+ (_001E).

series.title: Homeownership Rate by Race
series.description: Owner-occupied share of occupied housing units by race of householder (B25003), with Black/White and Hispanic/White gaps.

source.name: US Census Bureau, ACS 1-Year B25003 (+race iterations) via Census API

construction.method: homeownership_rate = B25003{su}_002E (owner-occupied) / B25003{su}_001E (total occupied) x 100.

series.title: Imprisonment Rate by Race
series.description: Sentenced prisoners per 100,000 US residents by race/ethnicity, 2010-2020, from BJS Prisoners in 2020 Figure 2. The widest measured disparity: Black rate ~5-6x White.

source.name: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Prisoners in 2020 (NCJ 302776), Fig. 2 (E. Ann Carson, 2021)

construction.method: Download the p20st spreadsheet bundle, extract p20stf02.csv (Figure 2 data), parse year rows into per-race rates; ratio = Black/White.

series.title: Employer Firms by Owner Race
series.description: Employer firms, employees, and annual payroll by owner race from the Annual Business Survey Company Summary, 2018-2021.

source.name: US Census Bureau, Annual Business Survey (ABS) Company Summary via Census API

construction.method: API pull of FIRMPDEMP/EMP/PAYANN by RACE_GROUP (30=White, 40=Black, 50=AIAN, 60=Asian, 70=NHPI, 91=Hispanic); share of firms vs RACE_GROUP=00 total. Race groups overlap Hispanic ethnicity, so shares legitimately sum to ~97-99%.

series.title: Median Income by Race by Metro (cross-section)
series.description: 2022 median household income for White (B19013A) and Black (B19013B) households by metro/micropolitan area, with gaps and ratios.

source.name: US Census Bureau, ACS 1-Year 2022 B19013A/B by metro area via Census API

construction.method: API pull for all metro/micropolitan geographies for both race iterations; join on geography; keep metros reporting both; compute Black/White ratio and dollar gap; sort by gap.

quality.notes: Some small metros show Black median income above White (ratio > 1); real ACS estimates, retained.

series.title: Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade: Annual Embarked/Disembarked
series.description: Annual slaves embarked and disembarked in the trans-Atlantic trade, 1514-1866, total and mainland North America, from 36,108 voyages.

source.name: SlaveVoyages.org, Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database (2019 release, tastdb-exp-2019)

construction.method: Voyage-level sums of imputed embarked (SLAXIMP) and disembarked (SLAMIMP) by year of arrival (YEARAM); North America = REGARR 20000-29999. Regional cumulative totals by broad arrival region.

series.title: Middle-Passage Mortality
series.description: Middle-passage mortality: (embarked - disembarked) per year and as a percent of embarked, 1514-1866.

source.name: Derived from SlaveVoyages TAST 2019 (see D1014)

construction.method: mortality_total = max(0, embarked_total - disembarked_total) per year; rate = mortality_total/embarked_total x 100.

series.title: International Inequality Comparison (cross-section)
series.description: 2022 snapshot comparing the US with peers on HDI, inequality-adjusted HDI and loss, World Bank Gini, and direct Black/White-type income ratios (US, Brazil, South Africa).

source.name: UNDP HDR 2023/24 Composite Indices; World Bank Gini (SI.POV.GINI); national statistics agencies (IBGE, StatsSA, US Census)
source.license: CC BY 3.0 IGO (UNDP); CC BY 4.0 (World Bank); national-agency figures cited per row

construction.method: Keyless UNDP CSV and World Bank API pulls for 10 countries; national Black/White income ratios added with per-row citations (IBGE, StatsSA, Census).

series.title: Reparations Estimates Comparison (cross-section)
series.description: Curated comparison of reparations estimates from four distinct methodologies: SCF-static counterfactual, Darity-Mullen, Craemer price- and wage-based, plus CA AB 3121 per-harm schedule.

source.name: Fed SCF 2022 (computed); Darity & Mullen (2020); Craemer et al. (2020); CA AB 3121 Task Force (2023)
source.license: Published literature; per-row URLs in output

construction.method: Curated table of published estimates (each labeled with methodology, base year, and source URL) alongside this project's SCF-static counterfactual (P31). Not a policy prescription.

series.title: Voter Turnout by Race (CPS Voting Supplement)
series.description: Weighted voter turnout by race for biennial election years 2010-2022, from CPS Voting and Registration supplement microdata.

source.name: US Census Bureau, CPS Voting and Registration Supplement via Census API

construction.method: Individual-level CPS microdata (PES1 voted, PTDTRACE race, PWCMPWGT weight, for=state:*); turnout = weighted share of PES1 in {1,2} answering 1, by race group. REQUIRES a Census API key (free).

quality.notes: CPS self-report inflates turnout levels ~5-10pp vs ballot counts; the racial GAP is the analytically meaningful metric. 2012 milestone: Black turnout (77.9%) exceeded White (70.8%).

series.title: Intergenerational Mobility by Race (Opportunity Atlas)
series.description: Mean adult family-income percentile (kfr) of children born 1978-1992 by race and parental income percentile (p25/p75/p100), with Black-White gaps and ratios.

source.name: Opportunity Insights / Opportunity Atlas, Table 5: national estimates by cohort (Chetty, Hendren, Jones, Porter 2018, QJE 133(2))

construction.method: Extract kfr_{race}_pooled_pXX columns for the three parent percentiles; gap and ratio Black vs White per cohort.

series.title: Federal Income Tax by AGI Bracket (cross-section)
series.description: IRS Statistics of Income Table 1.4 (tax year 2021): returns, AGI, and income tax by AGI bracket, with effective rates.

source.name: IRS Statistics of Income, Table 1.4 (All Returns by Size of AGI), Tax Year 2021

construction.method: Keyless download of the published .xls; parse bracket rows (returns, AGI, taxable income, tax); effective_rate = tax/AGI per bracket. REAL IRS data, no imputation.

series.title: Federal Tax Burden by Imputed Race (derived)
series.description: Effective federal income-tax rates by imputed race: IRS SOI brackets with racial composition imputed from ACS household income distributions (B19001A/B).

source.name: IRS SOI Table 1.4 (2021) + Census ACS 2022 B19001A/B via Census API

construction.method: For each AGI bracket, racial composition of households estimated from ACS B19001A/B income distributions and applied to IRS bracket tax amounts (standard demographic imputation as used by TPC/ITEP).

quality.notes: RACE IS IMPUTED: the IRS does not collect race. Households != tax returns; within-bracket composition assumed uniform. Effective-rate differences reflect the progressive code plus the racial income distribution, NOT differential treatment.

series.title: Black-White Wealth-Gap Decomposition (Oaxaca-Blinder)
series.description: Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition of the 2022 Black-White median wealth gap on SCF microdata: explained vs unexplained shares and driver composition.

source.name: Fed SCF 2022 microdata (see D1003)

construction.method: Oaxaca-Blinder on log net worth, White reference group, covariates (income, education, age, marital status, kids, labor force, homeowner); all five implicates weighted by WGT.

quality.notes: ~65% explained / 35% unexplained (log); leading explained drivers homeownership, education, age; income ~2%. Decomposition identities exact (residual=0).

series.title: Black-White Income-Gap Decomposition (explained share)
series.description: Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition of the 2022 Black-White household income gap on SCF microdata.

source.name: Fed SCF 2022 microdata (see D1003)

construction.method: Oaxaca-Blinder on log household income, White reference, human-capital + demographic covariates; weighted by WGT.

quality.notes: ~53% explained / 47% unexplained (log income). 'Unexplained' means unexplained conditional on included covariates -- it is NOT synonymous with discrimination.

series.title: Black-White Homeownership-Gap Decomposition (LPM)
series.description: Oaxaca-Blinder on a linear probability model of homeownership (SCF 2022): explained share of the ~44-point Black-White homeownership gap.

source.name: Fed SCF 2022 microdata (see D1003)

construction.method: LPM-Oaxaca-Blinder with homeowner indicator (HOUSECL==1); shares reported in percentage points of the gap.

quality.notes: ~44% explained / 56% unexplained; the unexplained residual maps to credit access, segregation, and down-payment constraints not observed in SCF.

series.title: Black/White Unemployment Cyclical Beta
series.description: OLS of Black unemployment on White unemployment (annual, 1972-2025): level beta, ratio slope, and recession-vs-expansion means. Shows the ~2x gap is a CONSTANT multiplier, not recession-widening.

source.name: Derived from BLS CPS via FRED (see D1005)

construction.method: u_B = a + b*u_W (OLS, level) plus ratio-series slope regression; COVID beta-shift computed with/without 2020.

series.title: Reparations: Aggregate Black-White Wealth Shortfall
series.description: SCF-static counterfactual: the dollar amount that would close today's observed Black-White wealth gap (median and mean basis), 2022.

source.name: Fed SCF 2022 microdata (see D1003)

construction.method: gap x Black households: (White median - Black median) x Black household count (weighted), and the mean-basis variant. Compare Darity-Mullen (a different, historical-compounding counterfactual) in D1017.

series.title: Incarceration Disparity-Attributable Annual Cost
series.description: Counterfactual annual fiscal + forgone-earnings cost of Black-White imprisonment-rate disparity, 2010-2019: excess imprisoned Black adults x per-inmate cost and earnings losses.

source.name: Derived: BJS imprisonment rates (D1011) x Census demographics (D1002) x BLS-based income assumptions

construction.method: (Black rate - White rate) x Black adults per year; x BJS-published per-inmate annual cost (~$45k) for fiscal cost; x earnings assumptions for forgone-income bounds. Every assumption labeled in output.
